basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 10.' and it opens 'VERS. 10.-- Qui ait: Vocem tuam audivi in paradiso, et timui, eo quod nudus essem, et'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 10.-- Qui ait: Vocem tuam audivi in paradiso, et timui, eo quod nudus essem, et abscondi me. Miserrimo genere respondit, quasi ideo possit displicere nudus, sicut eum fecerat. Ante peccatum | enim nuditatem suam non advertebat, quia ejus intentio in supernis erat. Nam quod se a Dei praesentia abscondi posse putabat, ei de insipientia poena peccati accidit, eum latere velle quem latere nihil potest.
